from.description: From is the template this one is derived from, by name.

packages.description:
Packages are installed with pkg -c into the clone. Empty is allowed and
means a plain copy, which is a reasonable thing to want.

release.description:
Release prepares from the FreeBSD mirror instead: fetch base.txz for
that release and build a template from it. Minutes of work, so this one
answers 202 and the client watches the template (JD-008). Empty with no
From means the host's own release, which is also the ceiling.

cpu.description: CPU is the number of virtual CPUs. Zero means 1.

cpuset.description:
CPUSet pins the guest's vCPUs to host CPUs, vCPU i to cpuset[i]: one
for each vCPU, each a different one (JD-041). Absent means unpinned.

image.description: Image is the VM image template the guest's disk is cloned from.

memory.description:
Memory is vm-bhyve's own form, a whole number of M or G: "512M",
"2G". Empty means 1G.

network.description: Network is a static address for that NIC. Absent means DHCP.

ssh_keys.description:
SSHKeys go into the default user's authorized_keys. A cloud image
has no password, so a guest with none is reachable only on its
console.

start.description: Start starts the guest once it is made.

switch.description:
Switch is the vm-bhyve switch the guest's one NIC is on. Empty means
no NIC at all.

autostart.description:
Autostart is whether the guest is in rc.conf's vm_list, which
rc.d/vm starts at boot. AutostartOrder is its place in that list,
from 1.

image.description: Image is what its disk was cloned from.

locked_by.description: LockedBy is the host named in the guest's run.lock.

vnc.description:
VNC is the address a running guest's framebuffer listens on, when it
has one.

autostart.description:
Autostart is whether the guest is in rc.conf's vm_list, which
rc.d/vm starts at boot. AutostartOrder is its place in that list,
from 1.

consoles.description:
Consoles maps a port to its device: "com1": "/dev/nmdm-web.1B". The
host side of the null-modem pair is the B end. Running guests only.

cpuset.description:
CPUSet is the host CPU each vCPU is pinned to, vCPU 0 first, read from
the guest's bhyve_options (JD-041). Absent for a guest not pinned, and
for one whose bhyve_options are not only a pin.

locked_by.description: LockedBy is the host named in the guest's run.lock.

memory_resident.description:
MemoryResident is the guest's resident memory in bytes, from bhyvectl.
Only a guest whose bhyve instance exists has one.

vnc.description:
VNC is the address a running guest's framebuffer listens on, when it
has one.

device_type.description: DeviceType is vm-bhyve's: file, zvol, sparse-zvol, custom or iscsi.

autostart.description:
Autostart is whether the guest is in rc.conf's vm_list, which
rc.d/vm starts at boot. AutostartOrder is its place in that list,
from 1.

changed.description:
Changed says whether this call changed anything on the host: true only
when it created the guest. Nothing here reconciles a guest towards a
spec (JD-016).

differences.description:
Differences is every setting the request and the guest disagree
about. A guest that differs is left as it is.

image.description: Image is what its disk was cloned from.

locked_by.description: LockedBy is the host named in the guest's run.lock.

vnc.description:
VNC is the address a running guest's framebuffer listens on, when it
has one.

problem.description:
Problem is vm-bhyve's own words for why it is not configured --
the same words Host Setup reports.

switches.description:
Switches are vm-bhyve's virtual switches by name, which a guest's NIC
can be put on (JD-038). Read only when vm-bhyve is ready; empty, not
absent, otherwise.

vm_bhyve.description: VMBhyve is ready, not_installed or not_configured.

device.description:
Device is the tap a running guest is using -- a new one on every
start (JD-019) -- and Bridge the bridge it is a member of.

autostart.description:
Autostart is whether the guest is in rc.conf's vm_list, which
rc.d/vm starts at boot. AutostartOrder is its place in that list,
from 1.

forced.description:
Forced is a stop that the guest did not answer within the deadline,
and that was powered off: the equivalent of pulling the plug, and
reported so that nobody mistakes it for a clean shutdown.

locked_by.description: LockedBy is the host named in the guest's run.lock.

vnc.description:
VNC is the address a running guest's framebuffer listens on, when it
has one.

address.description: Address is the guest's, with its prefix: "10.77.0.10/24".

Autostart is whether the guest is in rc.conf's vm_list, which
rc.d/vm starts at boot. AutostartOrder is its place in that list,
from 1.
